title: Pipeline conductor: loop termination, result anchoring, and stream-consistent tool fallbacks
creator: Sophie Chen
description: Problem: The current execution loop allows long multi-tool pipelines to: (1) accidentally re-enter the same tool chain due to result injection, (2) produce inconsistent streamed tokens vs final structured result, and (3) lack a robust mechanism to anchor intermediate tool outputs so downstream components can rely on them for idempotent retries. Goal: Implement a "pipeline conductor" layer that supervises multi-tool chains, enforces loop/recursion budgets, stamps and anchors tool results for safe injection, and guarantees stream-to-final consistency for structured outputs. This ticket covers design and implementation of runtime safeguards, streaming contracts, and a lightweight compatibility shim for older SDKs that don't implement the conductor protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline conductor API defined and implemented as a runtime module behind a feature flag
Tool results are stamped with a stable 'anchor id' that survives retry and is present in both streaming and final structured outputs
Recursion and loop budgets enforced: default depth 4, configurable per-organization; runaway chains trigger a graceful fallback response and audit log
Backward compatibility shim returns best-effort fallback messages for SDKs that don't understand anchor ids
End-to-end integration test verifying streamed tokens align with final structured payload for a 3-tool pipeline (generator -> web-fetch -> reranker)
Perf impact measured: <3% median latency regression on p95-critical path when conductor enabled
tasks: Spec: document pipeline conductor wire format and anchors (conductor-spec.md)
Runtime: implement conductor middleware that wraps executor loop
Tool SDK: add anchor extraction and injection helpers (js/py)
Safety: implement loop/recursion budget enforcement and audit events
Streaming: ensure partial events include anchor id and consistent JSON framing for structured outputs
Compatibility: add shim path in gateway for older SDKs (header: X-RW-Conductor-V)
Tests: unit + integration + chaos test (simulate tool crash + retry)
decisions: Use small stable 'anchor id' (RFC4122 v4 truncated to 12 chars) rather than full UUIDs to reduce token overhead in streams
Default recursion budget = 4 to balance expressivity vs runaway risk; enterprise customers can configure higher values via policy
Anchor stamping is performed by the first tool that produces a canonical structured fragment; subsequent tools may reference existing anchor ids but should not re-stamp

When budget exhausted, conductor returns a 200 with a structured error block and partial payload to preserve streaming compatibility rather than a hard 5xx to avoid user-facing downtime for composite flows

notes: Implementation pattern: conductor acts as a stateless coordinator — stamps anchors and emits audit events; stateful commitments (anchor -> canonical fragment) stored in KV with short TTL (default 12h)
Streaming contract: every partial 'chunk' event must include metadata: {anchor_id, seq, partial_checksum} so clients can correlate streaming tokens with final structured payloads
Idempotency: retries include X-RW-Anchor header; runtime will dedupe tool invocations if anchor_id + tool_name match an in-flight or recently committed result
Compatibility shim: when X-RW-Conductor-V is missing or older than 1, gateway returns 'conductor_compat' envelope with embedded best-effort anchor and a compatibility flag in the final payload
Edge cases: external tools that produce inconsistent JSON (malformed structured output) will cause the conductor to mark the anchor as 'noncanonical' and trigger rerun fallback policy
Observability: emit audit events: conductor.anchor.created, conductor.anchor.committed, conductor.budget.exhausted, conductor.fallback.invoked; map these to console dashboards
implementation_notes: Anchor ID format: base62(truncate(sha256(request_id + tool_name + timestamp)), 12) — deterministic but collision-resistant for in-flight dedupe
Budget plumbing: budget consumed on entry to a tool if tool invocation may spawn further executor cycles; budget refunded on short-circuit fallback to maintain predictable budgets across retries
Tests to add: - chaos test with tool that reinserts its own anchor (simulate infinite reinjection) - perf test measuring p50/p95 overhead with conductor on/off
qa_steps: Run integration pipeline: generator -> fetch -> reranker; verify stream events contain matching anchor_id and final structured output has same anchor_id
Simulate tool crash and retry; verify no duplicate tool side-effects when retry occurs with same anchor id
Set recursion budget to 2 for a user-level test case that attempts 5 nested tool calls; confirm budget_exhausted event and graceful fallback payload
risks: SDK adoption lag: older clients may not send conductor headers causing degraded anchor accuracy until shim is rolled out
Storage pressure: high-frequency microservices invoking many anchors could increase KV storage; mitigation: short TTL and sampling for audit events
Complexity: added coordination increases surface area for bugs; mitigate with targeted chaos tests and gradual rollout behind feature flag
